For the next six months, the dealership completely ghosted me. I followed up dozens of times with the new Service Manager, Troy Shane, and Johnny Aguilar. When the issue was finally escalated to the General Manager, Alexander Ayyoub, things became unprofessional.
After I exercised my right to file a BBB complaint due to their 6-month silence, Mr. Ayyoub sent me an email using intimidating and retaliatory language. He accused me of "bullying" for asking them to honor their own promise and explicitly stated he was "rescinding" a previous goodwill offer because I filed a complaint.
It is deeply concerning that a "luxury" dealership would admit to damaging a customer's vehicle and then use aggressive, hostile tactics to avoid paying a $500 deductible. If you value your car and your peace of mind, do not trust this management team. They do not stand behind their work, and they will turn on you the moment they make a mistake.
I am now forced to resolve this in Small Claims Court and through the California Attorney General’s office.

I am writing this to warn any potential customers of the gross negligence I experienced at Audi Beverly Hills Service. After paying $1,600 for service and full set of new tires, this service department released my vehicle in an incredibly dangerous condition that could have resulted in a fatal accident.

The Facts:
• Extreme Overinflation: I discovered that 3 out of 4 tires were inflated to 83 PSI. The manufacturer’s nominal pressure is 41 PSI and the absolute maximum rated pressure is 54 PSI.
• Immediate Failure: On the first day of driving, the fourth tire suffered a total failure, dropping to 7 PSI while I was on the road.
• Life-Threatening Risk: Driving on tires at nearly 200% of their recommended pressure is catastrophic. These were four ticking time bombs that could have blown at highway speeds.

The Response:
When confronted with this life-threatening error, Audi Beverly Hills service offered a mere $200 refund. This "solution" is an insult. It demonstrates that they value a human life at a $200 discount rather than taking accountability for a massive failure in basic safety protocols. There was no internal investigation and no serious concern for the fact that they sent a client onto the road in a compromised vehicle.

If I were managing Audi Beverly Hills, I would be humiliated by this lack of oversight. As a customer, I am appalled. If you value your safety and the safety of your family, take your vehicle elsewhere.

Reviews.Text: I had an excellent experience working with Steve Proto at Auto Mediator. After a luxury vehicle valued over $110,000 was declared a total loss, the insurance company significantly undervalued it using CCC comparables that failed to account for the MANUFAKTUR paint and custom interior. Steve thoroughly analyzed the build, properly documented the factory specifications, and successfully negotiated with the opposing appraiser to increase the valuation by over $13,000. Without his involvement, the vehicle would have been underwater with the finance company. If you are dealing with a high-end or exotic total loss dispute, Steve is absolutely the person you want on your side.

Steve P is extremely knowledgeable. He was able to advise me that my car had severe frame damage and he explained it very clearly to me as to what constituted the frame damage in my case. He answered all the emails and the numerous phone calls and text messages. His report was extremely thorough and he also calculated the loss of use. I was able to use this report and was able to settle both diminished value as well as loss of use for my car from Geico. I did have a lawyer to negotiate the values, but Steve's report was gold.

The price of the report was very easily worth it.

Steve is totally awesome. Very knowledgeable, patient, willing to help throughout the often LENGTHY process of getting diminished value paid out. Trust him, and stick to the process, and keep asking your adjustor to pay the diminished value claim.

I recently had the pleasure of working with Steve at Auto Mediator for a diminished value claim on my new Lexus. I must say their service was outstanding. Steve is incredibly knowledgeable and professional. He took the time to understand my needs and provided expert guidance.

With the Auto Mediator’s 51 page highly detailed report using straightforward methodology that can be substantiated, explained, and backed up by facts and data, no formulas, was enough to recover $9,200 for my diminished value claim. Reviews.Text: I recently had an incredible experience at Beverly Hills Cadillac purchasing my 2026 Cadillac Escalade Sport. My salesman, Robert, was knowledgeable, patient, and went above and beyond to answer all my questions without any pressure. He guided me through the features of the Escalade, highlighting its powerful performance and luxurious interior that perfectly suited my needs. The entire process, from test drive to financing, was seamless and efficient. I highly recommend Beverly Hills Cadillac and Robert for anyone in the market for a top-tier vehicle! Cadillac of Beverly Hills is exactly how a luxury dealership should operate. From the moment you walk in, everything feels professional, organized, and respectful of your time—no pressure, no games, no unnecessary back-and-forth.

Huge credit goes to Kevin, who made the entire experience smooth from start to finish. He was knowledgeable, straight to the point, and actually listened instead of trying to sell me something I didn’t want. Every question was answered clearly, every detail was handled properly, and the process felt effortless.

You can tell this dealership values long-term relationships, not just quick sales. If you’re in the market for a Cadillac and want a stress-free, professional experience, Cadillac of Beverly Hills—and especially Kevin—is where you should be.

I inquired about the vehicle’s availability on Thursday, spoke with Robert on Friday and shared the details of my trade-in, and on Saturday we were driving it home! We spent less than 1 hour at the dealership and they were very efficient. The manager Bill and Jay from finance are part of the praise as they helped to deliver an amazing experience. Unfortunately, no luck than I did a search and found one very close in Beverly Hills Cadillac. Decided to send a request chat online made an appointment for the following day via phone. I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience warrants transparency.

I dropped my vehicle off at this dealership in 11/2025 for what was initially presented as a routine repair with a short turnaround. That process ultimately lasted nearly four months.

Throughout that time:

• The dealership was unable to confirm the location of my vehicle for several days after drop-off. I had to visit in person and request that staff physically locate it.
• Communication was inconsistent and often inaccurate.
• I was informed a required part had not arrived and would take months on backorder. After contacting corporate myself, the part was shipped to the dealership within days. I ultimately had to inform the dealership that the part had arrived, as there appeared to be a lack of coordination between corporate and the service department.
• I had to repeatedly escalate simply to receive updates.

To be fair, my assigned advisor appeared to be doing what he could within the limitations of the system. However, the overall management, coordination, and oversight at this location are deeply concerning.

At pickup:

• I was charged to top off the loaner vehicle down to the gallon.
• My personal vehicle was returned to me on completely empty (I immediately had to refuel over 12 gallons).
• The vehicle was not cleaned, despite being told it would be prior to release.

Within the same day of pickup, the check engine light came on and the vehicle experienced hesitation under acceleration. I had to seek an external diagnostic scan to determine the issue. I am still monitoring the vehicle, as it does not yet feel fully resolved or confidently “out of the woods.”

Given the length of time the vehicle was in their possession, I would have expected a thorough quality check and road test before release.

This entire process required far more effort and oversight from me than any customer should have to expend simply to have their vehicle repaired.

The only positive aspect was being provided a loaner during the extended repair period.

Future customers should document everything and be prepared to advocate for themselves, as proactive communication and service follow-through appear inconsistent at this location.

During the inspection, I was never called or informed about any difficulty accessing the hood. Instead, the vehicle was returned to me without any disclosure of problems or damage. I left the dealership assuming everything was handled professionally.

To be clear: I cannot say exactly how the damage occurred, but the hood mechanism failed immediately after the vehicle was handled during the inspection process, and no damage was communicated to me at pickup. What concerns me most is not only the damage itself, but the lack of willingness to investigate or assist once the issue was reported. When a customer entrusts their vehicle to a dealership, there should be responsibility, documentation, and customer support if something goes wrong.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and improves internal procedures regarding communication, vehicle handling, and post-service accountability. At minimum, customers deserve honesty and a proper review when concerns arise.

I am extremely disappointed in how Lexus handled a serious safety issue.

My vehicle completely stalled while I was driving, creating a dangerous situation for me and my daughter. Because of this, the car was towed from my home in Thousand Oaks. At that time, dashboard warning lights were illuminated.

I was later told by Lexus Santa Monica that the warning lights had gone off, and I was instructed to drive the vehicle to them. After inspecting it, they claimed they could not find anything wrong with the car.

That response is unacceptable.

A vehicle that fully stalls while in motion is not safe, regardless of whether a fault code appears later or warning lights turn off. Being told “nothing is wrong” after an incident like that — and being expected to continue driving the car — shows a complete lack of concern for customer safety.

To make matters worse, I was left without proper support or reassurance during the process. For a $66,000 vehicle and a brand that markets itself on reliability and safety, this experience was deeply concerning.

I am not someone who leaves negative reviews lightly, but a car that stalls and then receives no meaningful explanation or resolution is something other customers deserve to know about. Lexus should have handled this with far more seriousness and care.

I have had multiple Volvos and not sure I will continue buying these cars based on the experience I’m having.  I have a  2019 xc60 t8 (hybrid)……very low mileage 32,014 and I have this hybrid system failure and weird grinding noise while driving.  I took it directly to the dealer because they’re supposed to be experts on their product.  They diagnosed it and I paid $1,817 to change the coolant pipe and flush /change the coolant.   Error codes were cleared and they test drove the car and deemed it safe. They even did the courtesy of dropping it off at my home because I was short on time and leaving on a road trip and had waited a week to get my car back.

Upon driving the car, almost right away we notice the error message and the grinding sound was even louder than before.  A separate problem with key fobs not locking and starting the car wasn’t even addressed.  I took it back …Klaus, my adviser apologized and said it was unacceptable.   Next he tells me there is a different coolant pipe that is pinched and it will be another $944 + tax to fix it.  Regarding the keys, the tiny plastic tab inside the each key fob were broken and could not  be repaired or switched out with another shell.  The charge for 2 new FOBS is $1,369 + tax!  This key problem seems to me like a design error…tiny plastic tabs breaking? The electronics and everything else works but because a little tab can’t put enough pressure on the battery the whole thing is for the garbage?!  It’s not like I lost my keys in a fire, they are perfectly fine expect for the little plastic tabs.  Online you can buy new key FOB shells for $179.  The dealer is charging their customers a fortune for the programing which they don’t make accessible to independent repair shops.  Why gouge your own customers in this petty way?  I wouldn’t expect that from VOLVO….Porsche yes….

Back to the coolant pipe. My previous car was a hybrid Cayenne with more mileage, and never had such problems.  Why didn’t they see the pinched pipe the first time?  Or did they pinch it accidentally when they put it back together.  Why didn’t they check all the pipes initially?  Is the car engineering that complicated that even when the service foreman is working directly with Volvo corp USA they can’t figure it out?  I understand I’m paying premium pricing for service from a Westside area dealership but I except them to be experts on their product.   I don’t want to pay over and over again for guess work while they change each hose one by one.

The way things have been handled I do not trust this Santa Monica dealership.  I’ve never had this kind of experience at other Volvo dealers in the area.  I don’t think my service advisor Klaus, was being honest about the car passing the test drive  before it was delivered to me.  First he said it was driven for 20 miles, in a later text he said my car had been test driven for at least 50-60 miles.  Which is it because the invoice shows the exact same mileage in and  out….  They should know how many miles it takes for the engine error light to recalibrate.  In any case there’s no denying the grinding/rubbing sound when the car was in motion never went away.

I wrote to the assistant service manger, and no response.  When I called to speak to the manager I was instead forwarded to Klaus.  I’m not even sure the service manager saw all my correspondence or if he did is just too important to speak to me.  Since there’s no direct email or extension number provided for the manager I’ve had to leave voicemail and emails on the dealership’s general inquiry line and inbox.  Hopefully I will hear back .   I generally don’t post negative review for little things but I think it’s important for potential customers to know how things are handled here. I myself always appreciate both positive and negative customer reviews and find them the most helpful in my decision making.  A
